summary: I wrote plan.md for a logging camp on a 40 × 34 block clearing beside a rutted road. It has a dark spruce-log bunkhouse with notched corners, a front porch and a stone cook chimney, plus a tall open sawmill (end facing the road, vent on the ridge, brick boiler stack). Both roof specs passed a dry run with no warnings. It reads as a lumber camp because the logs go in from a log pile at the front, pale sawn boards come out to a yard at the back, and the clearing is full of stumps. A dark spruce-log bunkhouse (cobble plinth, notched corners, porch, fieldstone chimney) beside an open pole-frame sawmill with a brick boiler stack, a log deck, lumber stacks and stumps. I appended elements.md (26 items) and the PALETTE, VOCABULARY (33 helpers), ROOMS and PARTS sections to plan.md, leaving the architect's sections and coordinates unchanged. The six parts split along trades: log shell, sawmill frame, roofs, fittings, chimneys and fires, grounds. I did not run any builds, so none of this has been rendered or walk-checked.

rooms.name: Bunkroom
rooms.purpose: Cold, cramped sleeping hall for the crew: double-decker bunks (bunkBed) along the west and south walls, footlockers, a washstand barrel, one lantern. Keep the loft ladder at (5,2..5,16) and the lane to the back door clear.
rooms.ways_in: partition doorway (10,2..3,13) from the mess; back door (7,2..3,17) to the woodshed

rooms.name: Mess and cook hall
rooms.purpose: Warm, loud, firelit hall: a long spruce table with benches down the middle (messTable), the hearth in the east wall (reserved cells 18,2..3,12..13, keep the cell in front clear), a plate rack on the north wall, a barrel and a flour chest.
rooms.ways_in: front door (13,2..3,8) from the porch; doorway (10,2..3,13) to the bunkroom

rooms.name: Loft
rooms.purpose: Foreman's bunk and stores under the steep roof: single beds, sacks and barrels, tools, one lantern on a rafter; tall pieces only at z=11..14. Lit by the two gable windows.
rooms.ways_in: ladder (5,2..5,16) up through the hatch at (5,5,16), landing cell (5,6,16)

rooms.name: Front porch
rooms.purpose: Covered plank porch: a bench by the door, boots and an axe rack, a barrel, a peg rail. Lanterns already hang at (12,3,6) and (14,3,6). Keep the lane x=13, z=5..8 clear.
rooms.ways_in: step (13,1,4) at the rail gap; front door (13,2..3,8) into the mess

rooms.name: Woodshed
rooms.purpose: Open lean-to: cordwood x=9..12 (grounds part stacks it), clear lane x=5..8 to the back door, a chopping stump, a kindling barrel. Rough and sheltered.
rooms.ways_in: bunkhouse back door (7,2..3,17) to (7,1,18); open on the south side

rooms.name: Sawmill hall
rooms.purpose: One tall open work floor: the saw carriage on x=28..30 is fixed, the filing bench and grindstone at (33..34,1,17..19), the boiler firebox on the east at (36,1,17..18), an offcuts barrel, tool shelf on the west half wall, iron-chain belt line, lanterns under the plate. Dim, warm and busy. Keep 1-wide lanes from the north opening to the south doorway (x=27) and to the filing bench.

concept_subject: A northern lumber camp in a cut-over spruce clearing, seen from a rutted logging road of brown dirt and gravel. On the left stands a long, low log bunkhouse of dark bark-on spruce logs on a grey cobblestone plinth. At its corners the logs cross and stick out past the walls, alternating with each course. A steep grey slate-shingle gable roof runs along the road, with a dark eave and pale stripped-spruce boards filling the two gable triangles. A covered plank porch runs along the front under a low shed roof on pale posts, with a simple spruce rail and two hanging lanterns either side of a spruce door. Shuttered square windows sit in the log walls. A chunky mossy fieldstone chimney rises outside the east gable, past the ridge, puffing cook smoke. Cordwood is stacked under the west eave, and an open woodshed lean-to sits at the back. To the right, separated by a dirt path, stands the taller sawmill: an open pole frame of pale stripped-spruce posts with knee braces and a heavy top beam. Its 45° grey slate gable faces the road, with a plank gable end, a small loft door and a SAWMILL sign, and a louvred vent runs along the ridge. Inside, the dark interior shows a saw carriage running from front to back. In front of the mill, a log deck of bark-on logs piled in a low pyramid on skids is ready to roll in. Against the mill's east side, a red-brick boiler stack with a dark band and a stepped cap sends a tall white column of smoke high above the camp. Behind the mill, three stacks of pale fresh-sawn birch boards with dark spacer strips stand in the lumber yard along dirt lanes. Stumps are scattered across patchy grass, coarse dirt and podzol. A chopping block sits by the back path, and tall dark spruce cones close in at the edges of the lot.
concept_size: 40 wide, 34 deep; a 1½-storey log bunkhouse (walls 6 high, ridge at y=14) and a mill hall of the same height (ridge at y=14), with smoke stacks up to y=19
concept_palette: Dominant: spruce_log (bark-on dark brown walls) and slate palette (cobbled deepslate, deepslate tile, tuff; grey roofs). Supporting: cobblestone and mossy_cobblestone (plinth, chimney), stripped_spruce_log and stripped_spruce_wood (pale gables, posts, plates), spruce_planks, dark_oak verges. Accent: birch_planks and birch_slab (lumber), bricks and deepslate_bricks (boiler stack), lantern and campfire light, spruce_leaves. Ground: grass_block, coarse_dirt, podzol, rooted_dirt, dirt_path, gravel.

parts.name: Bunkhouse log shell
parts.scope: Cobble plinth ring y=1 (plinthCourse), spruce_log courses y=2..5 x=4..18, z=8..17 with saddle notches (logCourse, saddleNotch), ground floor planks y=1 x=5..17 z=9..16, partition x=10 with doorway (10,2..3,13), loft floor y=5 with hatch air (5,5,16), porch deck/posts/rails/step (porchBay), west cordwood. All opening cells and hearth cells (18,2..3,12..13) left as air. No roof.

parts.name: Sawmill pole frame
parts.scope: Plank floor y=0 x=23..35 z=8..20, 12 stripped_spruce_log posts y=1..5 (millPost), knee braces (kneeBrace), top plate y=6 (topPlate), west half walls (halfWall), boarded south back with doorway x=28..30 (boardBay), saw carriage rails, log and stonecutter (sawCarriage). Gables left to the roof tool.

parts.name: Roofs
parts.scope: roof.json for the bunkhouse (cottage preset, keep box 19..20,1..17,12..13) and sawmill (granary preset, keep box 36..37,1..19,17..18) exactly as the architect specified, dry-run and fix warnings; hand-built porch shed roof (slabs y=5 z=6..7, stairs y=4 z=5) and woodshed shed roof with its x=5..12 beam at (y=3,z=21).

parts.name: Fittings
parts.scope: Doors (doorPair) at (13,2,8) and (7,2,17); glass_pane windows (paneWindow) per OPENINGS incl. loft windows; open-trapdoor shutters (shutterPair) per FACADES; porch and mill lanterns on chains (hangLantern); loft ladder (loftLadder); SAWMILL wall sign (wallSign) and mill loft door trapdoors.

parts.name: Chimneys, stacks and fires
parts.scope: Cook fieldstone stack (fieldstoneStack) x=19..20 z=12..13 to y=17 with lit campfire at (20,16,13); mess hearth firebox (hearthMouth) at (18,2..3,12..13) with lintel; red-brick boiler stack (brickStack) x=36..37 z=17..18 to y=19 with signal campfire over hay_block; boiler firebox (boilerFirebox) at (36,1,17..18); saw-filing bench (filingBench).

parts.name: Grounds, yard and woodshed
parts.scope: Ground patches over the lot (groundPatch), logging road and skid road ruts (ruts), camp and back paths (pathRun), log deck (logDeck), three lumber stacks (lumberStack), stumps and chopping block (stump), six standing spruces (spruceTree), woodshed posts and cordwood (leanToPost, cordwood), lamp posts (lampPost). Ground first, leaving footprints alone.

recruit.why: Saddle-notched corners with alternating protruding log ends, axis-correct bark-on courses, floors, partition and loft hatch
Open pole frame: posts, plates, knee braces and plank boarding, the carriage rails
Steep and 45-degree slate gables with verges and ridge monitor via the roof tool, plus hand-built shed roofs
Doors, panes, open-trapdoor shutters, loft ladder, hanging sign
Chain-hung lanterns on the porch and under the mill plate, lamp posts on the paths
Fieldstone cook stack, brick boiler stack with signal-fire plume, hearth and boiler fireboxes
Mossy cobble plinth courses and stack bands
Patchy clearing ground, ruts, paths, stumps, spruces, log deck and stickered lumber stacks
Bunks, mess table and the mill's work floor, each kept walkable
